title: BACE: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology - Biochemistry & Molecular Biology - Enzyme Kinetics
subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: In the Michaelis-Menten equation, what does the constant $K_m$ represent?
options: The maximum velocity of the reaction
The substrate concentration at which the reaction velocity is half of $V_{max}$
The turnover number of the enzyme
The concentration of enzyme active sites
questions.explain: $K_m$ (Michaelis constant) is defined as the substrate concentration at which the reaction rate is half of the maximum velocity ($V_{max}/2$). It is an inverse measure of the enzyme's affinity for the substrate.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: An enzyme has a $K_m$ of 2 mM for its substrate. If the substrate concentration is 2 mM, what is the reaction velocity ($V_0$)?
questions.explain: By definition, $K_m$ is the substrate concentration $[S]$ at which the reaction velocity is half the maximum velocity. Since $[S] = K_m = 2\ mM$, $V_0 = 0.5 \ V_{max}$.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: In a Lineweaver-Burk plot, the y-intercept is equal to:
questions.explain: The Lineweaver-Burk equation is $\frac{1}{V_0} = \frac{K_m}{V_{max}}\frac{1}{[S]} + \frac{1}{V_{max}}$. The y-intercept (when $1/[S] = 0$) is $1/V_{max}$.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: A competitive inhibitor affects enzyme kinetics by:
questions.explain: Competitive inhibitors bind to the active site, competing with the substrate. This increases the apparent $K_m$ (more substrate is needed to reach $V_{max}/2$) but does not alter $V_{max}$ because high substrate concentrations can outcompete the inhibitor.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: Calculate the catalytic efficiency of an enzyme given $k_{cat} = 200\ s^{-1}$ and $K_m = 50\ \mu M$.
questions.explain:
Catalytic efficiency is defined as $k_{cat} / K_m$. First convert units to be consistent (Molar). $K_m = 50\ \mu M = 50 \times 10^{-6}\ M = 5 \times 10^{-5}\ M$. 
Efficiency = $200 / (5 \times 10^{-5}) = 40 \times 10^5 = 4 \times 10^6\ M^{-1}s^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: If an enzyme reaction follows zero-order kinetics with respect to substrate, which of the following is true?
options: The rate is directly proportional to substrate concentration.
The active sites of the enzyme are saturated.
$K_m$ is much larger than the substrate concentration.
questions.explain: Zero-order kinetics occurs when $[S] \gg K_m$. At this point, the enzyme active sites are fully saturated with substrate, and the reaction proceeds at its maximum rate ($V_{max}$), independent of further increases in $[S]$.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: What happens to the $V_{max}$ and $K_m$ in the presence of a non-competitive inhibitor?
questions.explain: Non-competitive inhibitors bind to an allosteric site (not the active site), removing functional enzyme from the pool. This lowers the potential maximum rate ($V_{max}$ decreases) but does not change the affinity of the remaining active sites for the substrate ($K_m$ remains constant).
